items.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017
items.q: I said, 'Warren, our drummer, will be right there with you.'

ctx.x: That’s a good story. I’ve had occasion where I’ll give a price for a trio and then I’ll kick myself because the person will go, “Is that per man?” And that’s not what I meant, but well yes. It’s a little too late to do that.

Oh yeah. And you know you get some really fair people and then — and we were lucky enough in my band to find an angel, and this guy, his name was Max Corzilius. Max, when he worked at Dupont he figured out a way to effectively filter jet fuel. He explained it to me one time. But he had the presence of mind at a certain point when he got a little older, he left Dupont and took his patent with him and opened up his own factory to make © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

this filtered jet fuel, so he became immensely rich, oh my God. So he heard us one time and he said, “Boy I love your band,” he said, “do you guys ever play out here at Smithsonian?” I said, “No, no.” He got us booked at the Smithsonian for their Friday jazz things. And got us booked all over the east coast, Baltimore and a little place called Rock Hall where they had a jazz club. And when we started playing the jazz festival in Clearwater — we’re not there this year but I mean every, for a long time we played…
